title: Stack them up

brief.story: A torch runs a blue LED from three AA cells in a row, and the bench supply is switched off: this one runs on batteries alone. It's dark. The cells are new.
brief.goal: Light the blue LED at 10–25 mA from the three cells.

hints: Black probe on the − rail, red probe on the + end of each cell in turn. A stack in series should climb 1.5 V at every cell: 1.5, 3, 4.5 V.
The readings go 1.5 V, 0 V, 1.5 V: the middle cell takes the voltage back down. It's in backwards.
Click B2 and turn it round.
debrief: Cells in series add up, but only if they all face the same way: 1.5 + 1.5 + 1.5 = 4.5 V. One backwards cell subtracts instead, 1.5 − 1.5 + 1.5 = 1.5 V, half of what a blue LED needs just to start glowing. Going round the loop, the pushes and the drops always balance (Kirchhoff's voltage law): with the cell turned round, 4.5 V = 3.0 V for the LED + 1.5 V for R1, so (4.5 V − 3.0 V) ÷ 100 Ω = 15 mA.
